extracted.intended_audience: MetaPost users and TeX/ConTeXt/LuaTeX authors who create, debug, and import MetaPost graphics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing, previewing, debugging, and importing MetaPost graphics into documents and web pages, and for selecting numeric representations for MetaPost arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof sheet generation with mproof.tex
rubrics_metrics.description: To write a proof sheet for MetaPost output, call mproof.tex as tex mproof ⟨MetaPost output files⟩. The resulting .dvi file can be processed as usual; graphics are embedded so different prologues need not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass an explicit list of MetaPost output files (possibly from different inputs). On shells supporting POSIX patterns you may use patterns (e.g., tex mproof fig.?), but be aware shell expansion order and matching (fig.10 can conflict with patterns like fig.??).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of outputtemplate to avoid shell-pattern conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Make output file names more significant to avoid shell patterns matching source files (example: outputtemplate := "%j-%c.mps").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If numeric indices like fig.10 cause pattern matching issues, change outputtemplate so patterns like *.mps match only output files (e.g., tex mproof *.mps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof sheet generation with mpsproof.tex (pdf-capable)
rubrics_metrics.description: mpsproof.tex is similar to mproof.tex but can be run through pdfTEX to directly generate PDF files and provides command-line options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tex mpsproof \noheaders ⟨files⟩ to omit filenames/date/page numbers. Use pdftex mpsproof \bbox fig.1 (\bbox is alias for \encapsulate) to produce a file sized to a figure's bounding box (only one figure at a time with \bbox).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives for previewing MetaPost figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Other previewing tools exist outside the MetaPost distribution, such as the mptopdf bundle, the Perl script mpstoeps.pl, and an online compiler/viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See external tools (e.g., http://tlhiv.org/mppreview/) when built-in scripts are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter error message format and interactive prompt responses
rubrics_metrics.description: When MetaPost finds an error it prints a line beginning with '!' (the actual error), several context lines showing the input read so far, and a '?' prompt for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At '?' you can type: x to terminate and fix the file; h for a help message; ⟨return⟩ to proceed as best it can; ? to list available options. The context listing shows how much of each line has been read and identifies sources (e.g., l.17, macro->, or descriptive phrase).

rubrics_metrics.name: message / errmessage / errhelp semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: message writes a string to a new line on the terminal; errmessage writes a string preceded by '! ' and followed by '.' and appends some context; errhelp is used to provide help text that h shows after an errmessage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use errmessage for errors that should include context and errhelp to provide explanatory help strings; h at the prompt shows the most recent errhelp unless empty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show commands and transcript-file behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Error messages and responses to show commands are written into the transcript file (main input name .log). When tracingonline is at its default value of zero, some show commands print results in full detail only in the transcript file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect the .log transcript for full diagnostics if tracingonline is 0; set tracingonline > 0 to show more online output.

rubrics_metrics.name: showtoken / showvariable / showdependencies usage
rubrics_metrics.description: showtoken identifies tokens (primitives show as themselves; variables and vardef macros are shown as '=variable' or macro descriptions). showvariable lists variables whose names begin with listed tokens and shows more information. showdependencies prints dependent variables and how current linear equations make them depend on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use showtoken for token-level inspection, showvariable to inspect variable contents and macro info, and showdependencies to understand how equations determine variable values (useful for debugging 'Undefined x coordinate' issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tracingall and loggingall for verbose diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: tracingall prints a detailed listing of everything the interpreter is doing; loggingall produces the same information but writes it only to the transcript file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer loggingall when tracing output is voluminous so terminal is not overwhelmed; use tracingnone to turn off tracing output.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingcapsules: show temporary quantities (capsules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingcapsules is positive, the interpreter shows the values of temporary quantities (capsules) as they become known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable this when you need to inspect intermediate temporary computations during figure generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingchoices: show chosen Bézier control points for new paths
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingchoices is positive, the interpreter shows the Bézier control points of each new path when they are chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for diagnosing unexpected path shapes produced by path-fitting or auto-control-point choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingcommands: show commands before performance (and more at higher levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingcommands is positive the commands are shown before being performed; a setting >1 also shows tests and loops before expansion; >2 shows algebraic operations before execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase level to inspect macro expansion and algebraic computations for hard-to-find bugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingequations: show variables as they become known
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingequations is positive the interpreter shows each variable when it becomes known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to follow the resolution of equations and variable assignments step-by-step.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracinglostchars: warn about omitted characters in labels
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracinglostchars is positive, warnings are produced about characters omitted from a picture because they are not in the font used for labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to catch font glyph issues in label strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingmacros: show macros before they are expanded
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingmacros is positive the interpreter shows macros before expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps diagnose macro-expansion order and macro-related bugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingoutput: show pictures as they are shipped out as PostScript files
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingoutput is positive, pictures are shown as they are shipped out as PostScript files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to verify that the produced PostScript output corresponds to expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingrestores: show restores of symbols/internal variables
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingrestores is positive the interpreter shows symbols and internal variables as they are restored at the end of a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to detect scoping and group-related state restoration issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingspecs: show outlines generated when using a polygonal pen
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingspecs is positive the outlines generated when drawing with a polygonal pen are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable when debugging custom pen shapes and their outline generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingstats: show resource usage at end of job in transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingstats is positive the transcript file contains resource-usage statistics at the end of the job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to monitor and debug resource limitations or unexpected consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingtitles: show titles online when they appear
rubrics_metrics.description: When tracingtitles is positive titles are shown online when they appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to follow title output; combined with tracingonline this controls where such output appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracingonline: control whether show outputs appear online vs transcript-only
rubrics_metrics.description: tracingonline default 0 causes some show commands to print their results in full detail only in the transcript file; setting it positive shows more on the terminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set >0 if you want detailed diagnostics on the terminal as they occur, otherwise inspect the .log transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on vector graphics scaling and target size
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector graphics should be created with a rough target size in mind because scaling affects technical parameters like line width, arrow size, and fonts; scaling large will change the visual character and may not match document stroke widths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply only small post-processing scale factors to vector graphics and design graphics to match target document stroke widths and font sizes to avoid visual mismatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including MetaPost graphics into TeX documents (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: In TeX sources a 'magic macro' provided by the format or an external package reads bounding-box info and reserves space; the file reference is passed to the output driver which embeds the file at output time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand whether you are using DVI+driver or an engine with built-in PDF output and choose the appropriate inclusion method (see specific format entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain TeX inclusion: use \epsfbox for DVI route
rubrics_metrics.description: For Plain TEX + traditional TEX engine + DVI output driver, use the epsf package macro \epsfbox{⟨filename⟩} (e.g., \epsfbox{fig.1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pdfTEX users refer to the standalone macros of the mptopdf bundle.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX inclusion: use \includegraphics and .mps for pdfTEX
rubrics_metrics.description: For LaTeX with traditional TEX + DVI the graphics/graphicx package \includegraphics{⟨filename⟩} is used. With pdfTEX only files with .mps are recognized as purified EPS to be converted to PDF on-the-fly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set outputtemplate to produce .mps names (e.g., outputtemplate := "%j-%c.mps") and include full filename (\includegraphics{fig-1.mps}). This also works with dvips via EPS fallback.

rubrics_metrics.name: LuaTeX and mplib inline MetaPost code caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: LuaTeX can inline MetaPost code directly and fall back to the built-in mplib library, but mplib doesn't support verbatimtex/btex ... etex constructs currently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use luamplib and \mplibcode / \begin{mplibcode} ... \end{mplibcode} constructs for inlining where supported; avoid verbatimtex/btex constructs when relying on mplib.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConTeXt integration and macros
rubrics_metrics.description: ConTeXt provides \externalfigure[⟨filename⟩] for including external graphics and can inline MetaPost code via \startuseMPgraphic/\useMPgraphic; ConTeXt MkIV (based on LuaTeX) has tighter mplib integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ConTeXt's kernel support for advanced features like shading/transparency and automatic processing and prefer inline MetaPost where natural interfacing with document properties is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including MetaPost in troff (grops/.PSPIC)
rubrics_metrics.description: GNU troff can include PostScript files via the grops output processor. The -mpspic macro package provides .PSPIC fig.1 which includes fig.1 using its bounding box dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use .PSPIC fig.1 to include the image with natural height and width from the file's bounding box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding MetaPost output in web pages (SVG/PNG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed SVG with an
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set width/height to scale graphics; SVG/PNG can be edited in GIMP or Inkscape; consult HTML references for tag/attribute details and see Section 8.1 for font handling in SVG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the MetaPost number system (-numbersystem)
rubrics_metrics.description: The internal numeric representation is chosen by the command-line switch -numbersystem with argument scaled, double, binary, interval, or decimal. The argument is stored in the internal string variable numbersystem; assigning to it at run-time triggers an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the number system appropriate to required precision/range/semantics before running MetaPost; do not attempt to change numbersystem at run-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: scaled number system (default, fixed-point)
rubrics_metrics.description: scaled refers to 32-bit fixed-point arithmetic (default). Precision ~10 decimal digits (about 5 digits before and after decimal). All arithmetic operations are done in software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for typical MetaPost usage where default precision and performance are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: double number system (IEEE 64-bit floating point)
rubrics_metrics.description: double does IEEE 64-bit floating-point arithmetic (53-bit mantissa ≈ 15 decimal digits). Smallest/ largest values ~2.2e-308 and ~1.8e308; smallest difference 2^-53. Variable warningcheck is set to 252 in double mode. Arithmetic uses hardware FPU if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when greater range/precision and hardware acceleration are desired; be aware of floating-point rounding and finite precision limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: binary number system (arbitrary mantissa via MPFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: binary is similar to double but mantissa size is variable and controlled by numberprecision (1..1000, default 34 decimal digits ≈ 113 bits). Exponent range is large; arithmetic uses the MPFR library and is usually much slower than double.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switch to binary when double precision is insufficient; increase numberprecision for more digits at the cost of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: interval number system (MPFI) and semantics caution
rubrics_metrics.description: interval number system (MPFI) builds on MPFR and represents numbers as intervals [l,r]. Interval arithmetic semantics can be unintuitive (e.g., w*w vs w^2 differ for w spanning zero). Current MPFI implementation mimics MPFR functions and is not fully adapted to interval arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interval mode mainly to implement algorithms in MetaPost language; be cautious about function semantics vs set semantics and verify intended behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: decimal number system (base-10 arbitrary precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: decimal provides arbitrary precision floating-point arithmetic with base 10 using the decNumber library. It avoids binary representation rounding artifacts (e.g., exact 0.1) and is useful when decimal-exact results (e.g., financial calculations) are required. numberprecision controls digits (1..1000, default 34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decimal mode for calculations that must match human/decimal arithmetic exactly; expect slower arithmetic than binary/double.

rubrics_metrics.name: numberprecision and exponent ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: numberprecision (valid 1..1000, default 34) determines precision in binary and decimal modes; exponent in binary/decimal internal representation is an integer in the range [-9,999,999; +9,999,999].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune numberprecision to balance precision vs performance; be mindful of allowed ranges and performance cost for high precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific-notation input allowed in non-scaled systems
rubrics_metrics.description: In all number systems except scaled, numbers can be given in scientific notation (e.g., 1.23e4 is interpreted as 12300 rather than as the product of 1.23 and e[4]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scientific notation for large/small numbers when operating in double, binary, decimal, or interval modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the reference tables for built-in features and variable meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables 6–12 summarize built-in features (internal variables, string variables, other predefined variables, constants, operators, commands, and macros) and give page references and short descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tables for authoritative, quick lookup of primitives, macros and their types/meanings when writing or debugging MetaPost code.
